### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** A parser used to accept a language must identify the language/version, lexical rules and disambiguation policy it implements, and distinguish recognition from structure and interpretation.

**Claim class.** Conditional engineering property derived from formal mechanisms and their boundaries

**Bearer or subject.** A versioned grammar/lexer/parser configuration and finite input byte sequence.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Undocumented priority, lexer/parser disagreement, silently ignored suffixes, or treating deterministic syntax as settled stakeholder meaning.

**Mechanism.** Fix decoding, tokenization, start rule, end-of-input convention and ambiguity policy; check that parsing accepts exactly under that contract and reports the selected structure or alternatives.

**Mature or evolved form.** Retain an explicit accepted-language contract; choose LL/LR/GLR/PEG/scannerless mechanisms according to grammar and consumer, with error policy recorded.

**Expected payoff.** Reproducible language admission and a clear place to diagnose grammar/implementation disagreements.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Mechanistic/formal support: Language-definition and algorithm properties apply to the chosen grammar formalism; grammar equivalence or implementation correctness is not established for an arbitrary parser. No direct comparative engineering-payoff experiment for this whole reconstructed property is established.

**Decision or consumer.** Text has a language whose grouping or token boundaries affect a downstream execution, analysis or authoring decision.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Use an established structured format and its existing parser when a record schema suffices; a two-field data entry form does not need a custom grammar.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** Text has a language whose grouping or token boundaries affect a downstream execution, analysis or authoring decision.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Known non-trigger: The examined input is not being admitted syntactically and is not supplied to any parse-structure consumer. For example, a consumer receives an already established scalar value and makes no parsing/admission claim. Lower-cost option already recorded: Use an established structured format and its existing parser when a record schema suffices; a two-field data entry form does not need a custom grammar. Applicability and evidence limit: An existing structured-format parser or a small form validator remains applicable when it performs syntactic admission. It can establish P cheaply if its evidence covers full consumption, errors and the declared ambiguity policy; choosing an existing parser does not make A false.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** The intended syntactic language and its policy are specified; decoder and lexer are part of the boundary; semantic actions do not secretly change the recognizer contract.

**Environment and boundary.** Covers syntactic admission. Binding, typing, executable authorization and natural-language intent are separate.

**Scope and exclusions.** Language-definition and algorithm properties apply to the chosen grammar formalism; grammar equivalence or implementation correctness is not established for an arbitrary parser.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Source language definitions/theorems or tool contracts are authoritative only within their versioned scope. This reconstructed research property is not a normative requirement for any target.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Record exact input/model, language/tool version, dependencies, evaluator, observation method and source locators; separate constructed examples, source proofs and observed tool outcomes. Grammar version, lexical decoding, parse-action side effects, or consumption status unavailable; a timeout is UNKNOWN, not rejection.

**Strongest objection.** Choosing one parse can hide rather than resolve ambiguity; generalized and deterministic algorithms have materially different costs and recognized languages.

**Known failures and misuses.** Constructed: accepting the prefix 1 from 1 garbage under a whole-input contract fails; choosing (1-2)-3 does not establish that a stakeholder intended that arithmetic.

**Response or descendant form.** Retain an explicit accepted-language contract; choose LL/LR/GLR/PEG/scannerless mechanisms according to grammar and consumer, with error policy recorded.

**What changed and what did not.** Retained mechanism/bearer: Fix decoding, tokenization, start rule, end-of-input convention and ambiguity policy; check that parsing accepts exactly under that contract and reports the selected structure or alternatives. **Ceremony versus mechanism.** Label, syntax tree, annotation or passing exit code is ceremony unless the rule and its boundary are actually enforced. Use an established structured format and its existing parser when a record schema suffices; a two-field data entry form does not need a custom grammar.

**Review findings and disposition.** **Review passes.** EPLT-RV01; EPLT-RV02

**Relevant findings.** **Finding id.** EPLT-AD005

**Finding.** The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/15

**Finding id.** EPLT-AD006

**Finding.** Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/16

**Limit.** No listed finding is not a guarantee of correctness; reviewers and their sampled documentary checks are described in the validation report.

## EPLT-C0002 — Recovery and incremental parsing preserve acceptance distinctions

### Identity

**Property id.** EPLT-C0002

**Property name.** Recovery and incremental parsing preserve acceptance distinctions

**Lineage id.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY

**Property families.** grammar; editing; incrementality

**Record kind.** ENGINEERING_PROPERTY

**Parent ids.** None recorded.

**Alias or supersession ids.** None recorded.

**Discovery source ids.** EPLT-SA013; EPLT-SA014; EPLT-SA027; EPLT-SA059

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Interactive language tools require useful structure before a program is complete; recovery and incremental parsing extend batch-recognition priorities.

**Original terminology.** Error tokens, missing tokens, repair sequences, reusable syntax nodes.

**Original form.** Error tokens, missing tokens, repair sequences, reusable syntax nodes.

**Original problem.** A returned tree or absence of one error-node kind is mistaken for a valid complete program; cached structure hides a changed parse.

**Branch ids.** EPLT-BA02

**Influence or relation class.** DOCUMENTED_ANTECEDENT

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** EPLT-SA013

**Locator.** Syntax trees; syntax trivia; errors

**Role.** genealogical/theoretical context

**Bounded support.** Full source fidelity includes malformed input; semantic correctness is separate.

**Source id.** EPLT-SA014

**Review findings and disposition.** **Review passes.** EPLT-RV01; EPLT-RV02

**Relevant findings.** **Finding id.** EPLT-AD005

**Finding.** The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/15

**Finding id.** EPLT-AD006

**Finding.** Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/16

**Finding id.** EPLT-AD005

**Finding.** The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/15

**Finding id.** EPLT-AD006

**Finding.** Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/16

**Next discriminator.** Resolve references before/after and compare the declared binding correspondence; prove substitution/freshness lemmas for general transformations, test capture counterexamples for implementations. **Review findings and disposition.** **Review passes.** EPLT-RV01; EPLT-RV02

**Relevant findings.** **Finding id.** EPLT-AD005

**Finding.** The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/15

**Finding id.** EPLT-AD006

**Finding.** Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/16

**Review findings and disposition.** **Review passes.** EPLT-RV01; EPLT-RV02

**Relevant findings.** **Finding id.** EPLT-FD008

**Finding.** Several citation-ready entries print the mature modern claim but retain only the first three historical source links. Those displayed paths do not directly establish important parts of the printed claim, and one uses metadata-only Huet as though it supported a current transformation mechanism.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/7

**Finding id.** EPLT-AD005

**Finding.** The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/15

**Finding id.** EPLT-AD006

**Finding.** Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/16

**Limit.** No listed finding is not a guarantee of correctness; reviewers and their sampled documentary checks are described in the validation report.

**Review findings and disposition.** **Review passes.** EPLT-RV01; EPLT-RV02

**Relevant findings.** **Finding id.** EPLT-AD005

**Finding.** The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/15

**Finding id.** EPLT-AD006

**Finding.** Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/16

**Residual limits.** Damas–Milner theorem for its language, Wells undecidability for Curry-style System F and Mairson worst-case lower bound; no average performance or universal inference result.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** Label, syntax tree, annotation or passing exit code is ceremony unless the rule and its boundary are actually enforced. Explicit type annotations plus checking can be simpler for a small interface or a richer type theory; no principal inference claim is required.

**Retention rationale.** Retain fragment-specific completeness and principalness; use bidirectional/annotated or restricted inference where full inference is unavailable, with UNKNOWN on resource exhaustion. **Relevant findings.** **Finding id.** EPLT-FD002

**Finding.** The inspected foundations narrative stops after the semantics branch. It gives no substantive branch treatment of type systems or effects/resources/protocols, despite declaring B02–B08 coverage and 24 resolved properties. These records exist in a.json but C13 requires an integrated argument in the human report, not only ledger rows.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/1

**Finding id.** EPLT-AD003

**Finding.** The normalized access-level enum contradicts the actual inspected portions in several records. SB034, SB039 and SB064 are labeled RELEVANT_SECTIONS_INSPECTED although each explicitly records only abstract/metadata access and failed body retrieval. Conversely SA030 is METADATA_ONLY even though its cited 1994 source theorem/definition sections were inspected; only the separately mentioned 1999 version was metadata-only. The aggregate access counts therefore are not counts of the stated source access. The explanatory normalization note does not repair an inaccurate machine value.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/13

**Finding id.** EPLT-AD005

**Finding.** The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/15

**Finding id.** EPLT-AD006

**Finding.** Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/16

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Richer types can establish explicitly encoded value/relational obligations when their logic, termination and solver/kernel assumptions hold; the encoded specification still needs independent justification.

**Claim class.** Conditional engineering property derived from formal mechanisms and their boundaries

**Bearer or subject.** Program, formal specification/type, logical theory and proof/checking evidence.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** An inconsistent or incorrect specification is treated as intent; unchecked axioms, solver assumptions or divergence undermine the promised interpretation.

**Mechanism.** Check proof terms or discharge refinement entailments; use finite qualifiers/decidable theories for automation where appropriate.

**Mature or evolved form.** Match precision to named failure modes; separate specification validation from checking and prefer restricted automation or dynamic checks where sufficient.

**Expected payoff.** More precise encoded invariants such as bounds or length relationships can be enforced than by plain data-shape types.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Liquid Types evaluates qualifier-based checking on selected benchmark programs. Author-selected corpus; the original quicksort case with unclear invariants was excluded; no controlled human-usability or requirements-match result.

**Decision or consumer.** A named value-dependent invariant matters enough to warrant annotation/proof burden.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Ordinary algebraic types plus a local runtime bounds check are adequate when the remaining failure cost and frequency permit it.

**Finding.** The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Finding id.** EPLT-AD006

**Finding.** Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** A checked ownership/linearity discipline excludes its specified resource or alias failures only under the corresponding operational model and trusted escape contracts.

**Claim class.** Conditional engineering property derived from formal mechanisms and their boundaries

**Bearer or subject.** Values/references and their aliases over execution, plus the language checker and unsafe boundary.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Treating linearity as uniqueness, aliasing models as borrow checkers, or safe caller syntax as proof of a sound unsafe/FFI implementation.

**Mechanism.** Track use/consumption, borrow lifetimes and alias permissions; validate unsafe libraries semantically and distinguish static checker rules from runtime aliasing semantics.

**Mature or evolved form.** Separate static and dynamic models, verify abstraction boundaries, measure rejected patterns, and retain explicit current gaps rather than universalizing memory-safety slogans.

**Expected payoff.** Modeled use-after-free, conflicting access or multiple-consumption failures are ruled out within the verified fragment.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Tree Borrows reports 53.97% fewer model-violating tests than Stacked Borrows among 460,182 filtered passing tests; MoveLight checks 31 outcome tests. These are model compatibility and bounded conformance checks, not defect reduction, instruction-level correspondence or a proved safe-checker implication.

**Decision or consumer.** Resources have lifetime, ownership or aliasing obligations that matter to correctness or optimization.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Immutable shared values under managed memory may need no affine interface; tracing garbage collection can be adequate when predictable reclamation is unnecessary.

### Applicability and authority

**Finding.** Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. **Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Observation or measurement map.** Inspect local/global session definitions and semantics; Check theorem premises and inspect run evidence independently. Map these values into the rule without substituting a successful tool exit for semantic truth.

**Required evidence.** Endpoint roles, type environments, communication order and recursion are modeled; theorem-specific consistency/safety/guardedness/role conditions hold; external participants meet required premises. Required witness data: protocol_contract and progress_and_execution_evidence.

**Evaluator or reasoning procedure.** Check protocol and process derivations plus theorem-specific environment predicates; use concrete trace or monitor evidence for participant performance.

**Decidability and approximation.** The finite instance/trace checks described by the evaluator may be executable. Quantification over all programs, contexts or executions requires the source's restricted theorem/proof; finite testing is incomplete, and timeout yields UNKNOWN.

**Positive witness.** Constructed: one sender and matching receiver exchange the specified integer and both terminate under the closed synchronous model.

**Counterexample or failure witness.** Published: Scalas/Yoshida Example5.14 demonstrates a live context typing a non-live process with a stranded participant; an offline external receiver is a separate constructed implementation-boundary failure.

**Unknown conditions.** Peer behavior, network/fairness assumptions, protocol version or the required progress theorem evidence unavailable. Missing evidence is not evidence that the guard is false. If A is already known true, an unestablished model, premise, proof or coverage leaves the operational judgment UNKNOWN through P/E; if a fact needed to decide A itself is unknown, report A=UNKNOWN. Only an established false A permits INAPPLICABLE.

**Inapplicability conditions.** No protocol-state conformance or progress claim is made for communicating processes; for example, a standalone pure computation has no communicating protocol.

**False positive and false negative risks.** False positive: treating an incomplete boundary/proxy as the whole claim (Context liveness or a local type check is promoted to live execution despite subtyping, missing peers, network/runtime failure or unsupported composition.). False negative: rejecting a valid instance because a conservative analysis or restricted proof language cannot express it; distinguish analyzer rejection from demonstrated semantic failure.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** A checker that rejects everything, empty accepted corpus, erased error nodes, or an observation model that omits the disputed behavior can make apparent success vacuous. Classic multiparty consistency restrictions limit programs and historical proofs have gaps; a live type environment can type a non-live process under certain subtyping.

**Change invalidation rule.** Protocol/role/subtyping, channel semantics, participant implementation, recursion/fairness or runtime-failure policy changes.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Protocol annotations/projection, composition restrictions, subtyping checks, migration and external monitor/adaptor burden. Cheaper path: A small local request/response API may use runtime state checks and timeouts when a session calculus adds no material consumer benefit. Applicability and evidence limit: Runtime state checks for a simple request/response protocol can establish a properly scoped conformance claim while A is true. Timeouts may be adequate for a bounded failure-handling contract, but do not alone prove global progress or eventual successful response.

**Evidence ceiling.** Model-specific session theorems and published counterexample; no universal deadlock/liveness claim and no evidence of real external performance.

**Finding.** The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. **Finding id.** EPLT-AD006

**Finding.** Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Finding id.** EPLT-AD005

**Finding.** The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/15

**Finding id.** EPLT-AD006

**Finding.** Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/16

**Positive witness.** A valid refutation witness: Constructed: f(x:Int):Int = 0 is type correct and total but fails f(x)=x+1 at x=0.

**Counterexample or failure witness.** An ill-typed program with a wrong result is not a valid witness against the ordinary-well-typedness implication; the witness must actually satisfy the ordinary type judgment.

**Unknown conditions.** If external requirement R is absent or ambiguous, intended-function conformance is UNKNOWN regardless of typing. Missing evidence is not evidence that the guard is false. If A is already known true, an unestablished model, premise, proof or coverage leaves the operational judgment UNKNOWN through P/E; if a fact needed to decide A itself is unknown, report A=UNKNOWN. Only an established false A permits INAPPLICABLE.

**Inapplicability conditions.** Ordinary typing is not claimed to establish intended-function correctness; for example, types justify a shape/safety result and functional requirements are assessed separately.

**False positive and false negative risks.** False positive: treating an incomplete boundary/proxy as the whole claim (A total safe function returns the wrong integer, chooses a wrong branch, omits a required action or implements the wrong policy.). False negative: rejecting a valid instance because a conservative analysis or restricted proof language cannot express it; distinguish analyzer rejection from demonstrated semantic failure.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** A checker that rejects everything, empty accepted corpus, erased error nodes, or an observation model that omits the disputed behavior can make apparent success vacuous. Many distinct functions share the same ordinary type, including functions that disagree on every relevant requirement.

**Change invalidation rule.** A changed requirement can invalidate correctness while the ordinary type remains identical.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** False assurance and omitted requirement validation; richer proofs also cost specification/maintenance effort. Cheaper path: Keep ordinary types for shape/safety and add concrete examples, tests/contracts or a richer specification only for the functional obligations that matter. Applicability and evidence limit: Types plus targeted tests or contracts may support their separate bounded claims. If ordinary typing is still promoted to intended correctness, a cheap well-typed wrong-function witness can satisfy the refutation predicate; missing or ambiguous requirements leave the assessment UNKNOWN.

**Evidence ceiling.** A simple typed counterexample decisively rejects universality; does not quantify practical defect-prevention benefits.

**Finding id.** EPLT-AD006

**Finding.** Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

## EPLT-C0022 — Control-flow linearity when handlers compose with linear resources

### Identity

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Algebraic handlers expose continuations; their composition with linear resources reveals an obligation beyond counting occurrences of resource values.

**Original terminology.** Control-flow linearity, continuation resumption multiplicity, value linearity.

**Original form.** Control-flow linearity, continuation resumption multiplicity, value linearity.

**Original problem.** A multi-shot handler duplicates a continuation that writes/closes the same linear file twice; discarding a continuation can violate an exactly-once obligation.

**Influence or relation class.** DOCUMENTED_ANTECEDENT

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** EPLT-SA043

**Role.** genealogical/theoretical context

**Bounded support.** Value linearity alone misses duplicated continuations; control-flow linearity is a distinct composition condition.

**Source id.** EPLT-SA050

**Locator.** §4 Theorems 4.3–4.4; §5.1 implementation; benchmark discussion

**Role.** genealogical/theoretical context

**Finding.** The control-flow-linearity predicate turns linear-use safety into an unconditional eventual-resumption claim. It requires each relevant dynamic execution to resume a captured exactly-once continuation exactly once, while its scope explicitly includes admitted transitions/executions and its assumptions do not require completion, termination or discharge of all residual obligations. A safe prefix with a pending continuation therefore violates the literal predicate; a diverging or suspended computation can preserve every linearity invariant without ever resuming that continuation. Checking the combined typing derivation, the stated evaluator, cannot establish this extra liveness claim.

XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Finding.** Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Alternative mechanisms.** Garbage collection is adequate for irregular lifetimes without a strict reclamation constraint; stack allocation suffices for ordinary nonescaping locals.

**Positive witness.** Constructed: all nodes of a temporary parse arena are consumed before the arena is released and none escape to the result.

**Counterexample or failure witness.** Constructed: a returned closure dereferences a value in an already-released arena; alternatively a safe long-lived region retains many dead nodes, showing safety does not prove economy.

**Inapplicability conditions.** No value’s region lifetime is used to justify reclamation; for example, reclamation is justified solely by a separate tracing-GC contract and no region-lifetime claim is made.

**False positive and false negative risks.** False positive: treating an incomplete boundary/proxy as the whole claim (A reference escapes a deallocated region; an overly large region retains dead objects; safety theorem mistaken for optimal memory consumption.). False negative: rejecting a valid instance because a conservative analysis or restricted proof language cannot express it; distinguish analyzer rejection from demonstrated semantic failure.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** A checker that rejects everything, empty accepted corpus, erased error nodes, or an observation model that omits the disputed behavior can make apparent success vacuous. Bulk reclamation is coarser than per-cell liveness and may retain memory; combining regions and garbage collection has additional dangling-pointer obligations.

**Change invalidation rule.** Lifetime/escape, region grouping, foreign references, control flow, allocation policy or runtime representation changes.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Region annotations/inference, memory retained until region end, frequent small region operations and interaction with GC/FFI. Cheaper path: Garbage collection is adequate for irregular lifetimes without a strict reclamation constraint; stack allocation suffices for ordinary nonescaping locals. Applicability and evidence limit: Stack allocation for nonescaping locals is a small region/lifetime argument when lifetime justifies reclamation, so A remains true. A direct nonescape/live-use argument can satisfy P cheaply. Choosing GC is a no-trigger route only if the region-lifetime justification is actually absent.

**Finding.** Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. ### Claim and mechanism

**Mature or evolved form.** Use permission-aware typestate, restrict strong updates, add dynamic checks at open boundaries, or use a simpler state machine where static tracking adds little.

## EPLT-C0101 — Choose and validate IR invariants for their semantic consumer

### Identity

**Property id.** EPLT-C0101

**Property name.** Choose and validate IR invariants for their semantic consumer

**Lineage id.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY

**Property families.** B09 Intermediate representations

**Record kind.** GUARDED_ENGINEERING_PROPERTY

**Parent ids.** None recorded.

**Alias or supersession ids.** None recorded.

**Discovery source ids.** EPLT-SB001; EPLT-SB002; EPLT-SB003; EPLT-SB004; EPLT-SB005; EPLT-SB007

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** SSA made unique definitions and merge points explicit (Cytron et al. 1991); ANF/CPS and typed assembly pursued different control/type consumers. MLIR and its 2025 semantic-dialect work extend the multi-representation branch.

**Original terminology.** SSA; phi-functions; administrative normal form; CPS; typed assembly; operation legality

**Original form.** Represent control/dataflow or retained type information so an analysis or pass can use an explicit invariant.

**Original problem.** A pass receives a representation whose dominance, effects, numeric semantics or metadata assumptions it silently misreads.

**Branch ids.** EPLT-BB01

**Influence or relation class.** REFINEMENT_OR_RESTRICTION

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** EPLT-SB003

**Locator.** Introduction and definitions of SSA, dominance frontiers and phi placement

**Source id.** EPLT-SB004

**Locator.** Retrospective opening pages: CPS history, administrative reductions and reactions

**Source id.** EPLT-SB005

**Locator.** §7.3 type safety; typed CPS and closure conversion

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Do not project current features, proof coverage or terminology backwards onto earlier versions.

**Relation class explanation.** Detailed dated historical/analytical edges are in genealogy_edges; this record summarizes qualified present evolution and does not claim every cited source influenced every other source.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** A useful IR contract states the invariant actually needed by the next consumer and separately establishes any semantic correspondence claimed for lowering.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_DESCRIPTIVE_AND_ENGINEERING

**Bearer or subject.** intermediate representation and its producer/consumer invariants

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** A pass receives a representation whose dominance, effects, numeric semantics or metadata assumptions it silently misreads.

**Mechanism.** Identify the region/operation semantics, verify structural invariants and connect input/output meanings with a typed elaboration or preservation relation. Multiple purpose-specific IRs can reduce each pass’s proof burden.

**Mature or evolved form.** Typed intermediate pipelines and MLIR legality interfaces are complemented by explicit semantic lowerings and independent translation/transfer checks.

**Expected payoff.** Expose malformed inputs early and make pass obligations local and checkable.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** SSA construction and TAL safety are formal results; MLIR2025 reports concrete poison-related miscompilations exposed by semantic validation, beyond structural acceptance.

**Decision or consumer.** An analysis, optimizer, lowering pass or diagnostic tool operating on a named IR.

**Alternative mechanisms.** One simple AST plus interpreter for a small language; multiple IRs for distinct consumers; validated direct lowering instead of a universal canonical IR.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A transformation or analysis depends on representational invariants that are not guaranteed by parsing alone.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Known non-trigger: No transformation or analysis depends on representation invariants beyond parsing; for example, the only task is syntactic recognition with no downstream invariant-dependent analysis. Lower-cost option already recorded: For a small expression evaluator with no control-flow optimization, retain one well-specified AST and validate its constructors; building SSA and multiple dialects adds no necessary guarantee. Applicability and evidence limit: A single well-specified AST with validated constructors can establish the required applicable representation invariants. SSA and multiple dialects are not necessary merely because A is true. Constructor validity alone does not prove semantic preservation.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** The consumer’s real preconditions are enumerated; containing operations define region meaning; well-formedness and semantic preservation are separately stated.

**Environment and boundary.** Parsed AST → elaborated or typed IR → transformed IR. Executable code and external intent are further boundaries.

**Scope and exclusions.** Structural invariants, type/effect obligations and semantic relations of identified IR fragments. Excludes: Universal optimal representation, full source-map fidelity, or external requirement correctness from verifier acceptance.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Conditional semantic/mechanistic result. No universal mandate or legal authority is inferred.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** IR/semantics versions, verifier mode/output, transformation identities and proof or validator evidence for each claimed semantic step.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** EPLT-C0102 resolves elaboration choices; EPLT-C0103 consumes IR semantics; EPLT-C0104/EPLT-C0108 establish transformations; EPLT-C0114 revalidates changed dialect meanings.

**Failure of assumptions.** A structurally legal operation with wrong denotation passes verification; graph regions wrongly treated as SSA CFGs can be rejected or transformed incorrectly.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Each IR adds converters, invariants, diagnostics, source-location propagation and maintenance during language evolution.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Re-enter when operation/region semantics, verifier, type/effect rule, lowering or diagnostic/source-map contract changes; retire unused intermediate forms only after consumer obligations migrate.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** EPLT-KB01

**Strongest objection.** A valid typed or SSA artifact can compute the wrong thing, and forcing all consumers into one canonical IR can discard needed information or inflate proof/diagnostic cost.

**Known failures and misuses.** Published MLIR2025 select rewrite remained syntactically valid yet introduced poison from the unchosen operand. Constructed: a well-typed addition op replacing intended subtraction also passes an IR verifier.

**Response or descendant form.** Typed intermediate pipelines and MLIR legality interfaces are complemented by explicit semantic lowerings and independent translation/transfer checks.

**What changed and what did not.** Newer semantic tooling checks meaning in addition to structure; it does not make every dialect or pass verified.

**Residual limits.** Operation semantics, effect/alias information and source diagnostics may be incomplete; prototype fragment coverage remains limited.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** An IR diagram, verifier badge or extra lowering stage is useful only if a consumer uses its stated invariant.

**Internal tension ids.** None recorded.

**Retention status.** CONTEXT_DEPENDENT

**Retention rationale.** Retain consumer-specific contracts and evidence boundaries; reject a universal canonicalization or verification-by-typing inference.

### Predicates, witnesses and evaluation

**Predicate specifications.** **Predicate id.** EPLT-C0101-P01

**Property id.** EPLT-C0101

**Name and plain language claim.** A useful IR contract states the invariant actually needed by the next consumer and separately establishes any semantic correspondence claimed for lowering.

**Predicate kind.** SYNTACTIC_OR_WELL_FORMEDNESS_RULE

**Subject and argument signature.** IRContract(r, consumer, semantics, checker)

**Variable domains and units.** r is a finite IR artifact; consumer/checker are versioned programs; invariants and semantic relations are predicates, not counts.

**Quantifiers and scope.** For each admitted r and each precondition the consumer relies on; universal behavior only when an additional semantic theorem supplies it.

**State trace event or model bearer.** intermediate representation and its producer/consumer invariants

**Temporal and modal semantics.** Whole execution behavior unless the explicit relation below restricts the observation to states or finite traces.

**Assumptions.** The consumer’s real preconditions are enumerated; containing operations define region meaning; well-formedness and semantic preservation are separately stated.

**Applicability guard.** A transformation or analysis depends on representational invariants that are not guaranteed by parsing alone.

**Expression or precise operational rule.** **A.** A transformation or analysis depends on representational invariants that are not guaranteed by parsing alone.

**P.** WellFormed_IR(r) ∧ ConsumerPreconditions(r); any claim Preserve(lower,r) additionally requires ObsTarget(lower(r)) related to ObsSource(r). WellFormed alone does not imply Preserve.

**E.** IR/semantics versions, verifier mode/output, transformation identities and proof or validator evidence for each claimed semantic step.

**Verdict rule.** Evaluate A (applicability), P (claim truth) and E (evidence adequacy) separately. A=FAIL gives INAPPLICABLE, never a vacuous pass. A=UNKNOWN or required E missing gives UNKNOWN. For A=PASS, sound proof/complete scoped check supports PASS; a valid scoped counterexample gives FAIL; timeout, unsupported features, heuristic failure or incomplete coverage give UNKNOWN. E=FAIL denotes a known mismatch between evidence and bearer, not automatic semantic falsity.

**Source of the expression.** Researcher operational reconstruction of the cited semantic relation; source theorem limits remain explicit.

**Observation or measurement map.** Map operations, control/dataflow and type/effect annotations to their declared meanings; source locations are diagnostic provenance, not semantics by default.

**Required evidence.** IR/semantics versions, verifier mode/output, transformation identities and proof or validator evidence for each claimed semantic step.

**Evaluator or reasoning procedure.** Run/review the correct verifier against the consumer contract, then separately check the semantic relation if claimed.

**Decidability and approximation.** Finite structural verification is often decidable. Semantic equivalence of general programs is not; bounded validation has bounded scope.

**Positive witness or worked example.** Constructed: SSA merge uses phi operands from the appropriate predecessors; the consumer sees one reaching definition and a proved lowering relates the merge to source branch behavior.

**Negative witness or counterexample.** Published MLIR2025 select rewrite remained syntactically valid yet introduced poison from the unchosen operand. Constructed: a well-typed addition op replacing intended subtraction also passes an IR verifier.

### Evidence limits and open questions

**Evidence ceiling.** Fragment-specific invariants and semantic checks; no theorem of whole-toolchain or intent correctness.

**Transferability limits.** Applicable to another language/tool only after re-establishing its semantics, relation, assumptions and implementation correspondence.

**Unverified or open questions.** Comparative maintenance and diagnostic costs for a particular IR decomposition remain application-specific.

**Next discriminator.** Give the consumer a structurally legal artifact that violates a semantic assumption; check whether the separate semantic gate detects it.

**Review findings and disposition.** **Review passes.** EPLT-RV01; EPLT-RV02

**Relevant findings.** **Finding id.** EPLT-AD006

**Finding.** Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Full history locator.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY_RESEARCH_COVERAGE_LEDGER.json#/reviews/FINDINGS/16

## EPLT-C0102 — Make elaboration choices explicit and justify coherence where meaning must be unique

### Identity

**Property id.** EPLT-C0102

**Property name.** Make elaboration choices explicit and justify coherence where meaning must be unique

**Lineage id.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY

**Property families.** B09 Typed elaboration

**Record kind.** GUARDED_ENGINEERING_PROPERTY

**Parent ids.** None recorded.

**Alias or supersession ids.** None recorded.

**Discovery source ids.** EPLT-SB004; EPLT-SB005; EPLT-SB006; EPLT-SB002

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Dictionary/evidence translations for qualified types exposed dependence on typing derivations; Jones1993 proves a sufficient coherence condition. Typed intermediate compilation retains enough structure for later safety arguments.

**Original terminology.** Qualified types; evidence translation; coherence; principal type; dictionary passing

**Original form.** Relate implicit source typing to explicit evidence-bearing target terms and show compatible derivations denote equivalent targets.

**Original problem.** The same accepted source expression can elaborate through different overload/coercion choices into observably different behavior.

**Branch ids.** EPLT-BB01

**Influence or relation class.** REFINEMENT_OR_RESTRICTION

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** EPLT-SB004

**Locator.** Retrospective opening pages: CPS history, administrative reductions and reactions

**Source id.** EPLT-SB005

**Locator.** §7.3 type safety; typed CPS and closure conversion

**Source id.** EPLT-SB006

**Locator.** §2 ambiguous out(in x); §7.1 uniqueness of evidence; §7.2 Theorem 5

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Do not project current features, proof coverage or terminology backwards onto earlier versions.

**Relation class explanation.** Detailed dated historical/analytical edges are in genealogy_edges; this record summarizes qualified present evolution and does not claim every cited source influenced every other source.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** When a language promises derivation-independent meaning, its elaboration must either choose a specified interpretation or establish coherence for the admitted derivations.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_DESCRIPTIVE_AND_ENGINEERING

**Bearer or subject.** source phrase, elaboration derivation and explicit target program

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** The same accepted source expression can elaborate through different overload/coercion choices into observably different behavior.

**Mechanism.** Record resolution rules/evidence and prove the translations equivalent under the chosen observation; reject, annotate or resolve ambiguous cases with a specified policy.

**Mature or evolved form.** Explicit core languages and checked lowering make choices inspectable; sufficiency conditions must be revised for extensions such as overlapping evidence or effects.

**Expected payoff.** Avoid hidden meaning changes caused by inference order or accidental dictionary selection.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Jones Theorem5 establishes equivalence under unambiguous principal types and evidence equality assumptions; TAL supplies a distinct type-preservation payoff.

**Decision or consumer.** The language implementer and user relying on a stable interpretation across elaborators.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Explicit overload annotations or deterministic specified resolution; direct monomorphic core; conservative rejection of ambiguous source.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** An accepted source admits multiple elaboration/typing derivations and the language claims a unique observable meaning.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Known non-trigger: The accepted source does not admit multiple elaboration/typing derivations, or no unique observable meaning is claimed for those alternatives; for example, a declared nonoverloaded core has exactly one admitted elaboration. Lower-cost option already recorded: An explicitly typed, non-overloaded arithmetic core with one specified elaboration needs no general qualified-type coherence machinery. Applicability and evidence limit: A specified resolution policy may cheaply settle the applicable ambiguity under the rule’s explicit policy alternative. Merely selecting one result does not establish coherence of all previously admitted derivations. A genuine single-elaboration language is the separate no-trigger case.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** The target equality/observation is defined; evidence entailment is coherent; ambiguity restriction and extensions match the proved language.

**Environment and boundary.** Implicit syntax/type derivation to explicit core term; type preservation and functional equivalence are distinct obligations.

**Scope and exclusions.** Coherence within the admitted type/evidence system. Excludes: All overloaded programs, arbitrary implicit conversions, or specification-intent correctness.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Conditional semantic/mechanistic result. No universal mandate or legal authority is inferred.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Source term, derivations/resolution traces, environment versions, definition of target equality and theorem premises.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** EPLT-C0101 carries explicit elaborated artifacts; EPLT-C0114 must recheck resolution-policy changes; EPLT-C0104 respects evaluation effects introduced by coercions.

**Failure of assumptions.** Overlapping inequivalent evidence or ambiguous type variables defeats derivation independence; rejection may also exclude harmless cases.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Annotations, evidence tracking and proof obligations grow with extensions; conservative ambiguity checks burden expressiveness.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Re-enter on new instances/coercions, imports, evidence equality, defaulting or inference rules; obsolete proofs retain historical scope.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** EPLT-KB02

**Strongest objection.** Explicit evidence alone does not ensure unique meaning; a decidable sufficient coherence criterion can be restrictive, and language extensions can invalidate it.

**Known failures and misuses.** Jones §2 out(in x) has an ambiguous ∀a.C a⇒Int scheme; distinct evidence can distinguish translations. Conversely his []==[] discussion shows conservative ambiguity rejection can exclude an intuitively coherent term.

**Response or descendant form.** Explicit core languages and checked lowering make choices inspectable; sufficiency conditions must be revised for extensions such as overlapping evidence or effects.

**What changed and what did not.** Evidence-bearing targets make choices visible and proofs precise; coherence remains relative to permitted evidence and observations.

**Residual limits.** A specified deterministic resolver can be stable yet select an unintended meaning; no user-intent guarantee follows.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** Recording every internal derivation adds overhead unless coherence, diagnostics, caching or reproducibility consumes it.

**Internal tension ids.** None recorded.

**Retention status.** RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM

**Retention rationale.** Retain explicit choice and scoped coherence; allow specified resolution or annotations as cheaper alternatives.

## EPLT-C0103 — Use sound semantic overapproximation with explicit precision, coverage and convergence limits

### Identity

**Property id.** EPLT-C0103

**Property name.** Use sound semantic overapproximation with explicit precision, coverage and convergence limits

**Lineage id.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY

**Property families.** B10 Analysis and abstract interpretation

**Record kind.** GUARDED_ENGINEERING_PROPERTY

**Parent ids.** None recorded.

**Alias or supersession ids.** None recorded.

**Discovery source ids.** EPLT-SB014; EPLT-SB015; EPLT-SB016; EPLT-SB017; EPLT-SB007; EPLT-SB051

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Cousot/Cousot1977 unified dataflow through semantic approximation; later frameworks separated choices of abstraction and convergence. Astrée specialized domains to applications; soundiness accepts explicit missed behaviors; 2025/2026 work checks generated transfer functions.

**Original terminology.** Collecting semantics; abstract domain; fixpoint; widening/narrowing; reduced product; soundiness

**Original form.** Compute a tractable overapproximation of concrete reachable states or traces and discharge a property using that superset.

**Original problem.** A pattern detector or incomplete model is mistaken for proof that a program has no bad execution; precise analysis may fail to terminate or scale.

**Branch ids.** EPLT-BB02

**Influence or relation class.** REFINEMENT_OR_RESTRICTION

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** EPLT-SB014

**Locator.** Author summary: fixpoints, abstractions and antecedents

**Source id.** EPLT-SB015

**Locator.** Collecting semantics; Proposition 4.3; extrapolation; Galois-connection formulations

**Source id.** EPLT-SB016

**Locator.** Language restrictions; reduced product; widening; application experience

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Do not project current features, proof coverage or terminology backwards onto earlier versions.

**Relation class explanation.** Detailed dated historical/analytical edges are in genealogy_edges; this record summarizes qualified present evolution and does not claim every cited source influenced every other source.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** An absence-of-bad-behavior conclusion requires a sound abstraction of all relevant concrete behavior, a validated fixpoint/postfixpoint, and exclusion of the bad set; unknowns and deliberate omissions remain explicit.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_DESCRIPTIVE_AND_ENGINEERING

**Bearer or subject.** concrete semantics, abstract domain and computed invariant

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** A pattern detector or incomplete model is mistaken for proof that a program has no bad execution; precise analysis may fail to terminate or scale.

**Mechanism.** Specify concrete semantics and concretization; use sound transfer functions and inductive abstract invariants, with widening/narrowing or a finite domain to control convergence.

**Mature or evolved form.** Reduced products, relational/context/path-sensitive domains and checked transfer-function generation improve precision selectively; underapproximating bug finders remain a different service.

**Expected payoff.** Prove scoped safety while balancing false alarms, runtime and domain-maintenance cost.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Astrée reports application-specific success; MLIR2025 verifies transfers; SAIL2026 generates checked NN transformers. These do not establish universally superior precision or labor savings.

**Decision or consumer.** A compiler selecting a rewrite or a verifier concluding a safety property.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Cheap syntactic checks for purely syntactic requirements; testing or underapproximation for bug finding; bounded symbolic/model checking with explicit bounds.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A consumer wants absence of a semantic bad behavior over a specified program/input class, or relies on an analysis fact to transform code.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Known non-trigger: Neither absence of semantic bad behavior over a program/input class nor an analysis fact used for a semantic rewrite is claimed; for example, only identifier spelling is checked. Lower-cost option already recorded: To enforce “identifier must match this spelling rule,” a parser/lexical check is adequate; an abstract interpreter adds no semantic benefit. Applicability and evidence limit: An exact finite analysis may cheaply establish the applicable semantic absence claim when its domain and coverage are complete. A lexical spelling check supports only its lexical target; it is no-trigger only when no semantic-absence or rewrite justification is attached.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Concrete operations/environment are modeled; γ and transfers are sound for supported features; initial states covered; fixpoint computation and checker implement their stated rules.

**Environment and boundary.** Source/IR/bytecode/binary analyses have different semantic inputs; upstream/downstream correctness is not implicit.

**Scope and exclusions.** Safety over the modeled input/state/trace set and supported operations. Excludes: Completeness, absence of false alarms, omitted reflection/native behavior, termination or intent correctness unless separately proved.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Conditional semantic/mechanistic result. No universal mandate or legal authority is inferred.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Versioned concrete/abstract semantics, inclusion/soundness proof, input assumptions, supported-feature inventory, convergence result and checker identity.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** EPLT-C0101 supplies faithful IR; EPLT-C0104 may use proven premises; EPLT-C0115 invalidates stale facts; EPLT-C0116 checks model/runtime correspondence.

**Failure of assumptions.** Ignoring eval/native code can miss a bad behavior. A sampled loss of zero need not mean global soundness; SAIL uses a separate verifier or manual proof.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Relational/context/path precision can explode; widening loses information; languages and libraries require model upkeep. A fallback top element remains sound but may be unhelpful.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Recompute/check when concrete semantics, initial assumptions, libraries, abstractions, transfer functions or widening policy changes; retire unused analysis precision.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** EPLT-KB03; EPLT-KB18

**Strongest objection.** Soundness can coexist with useless top results, and good practical bug finding can be intentionally unsound; model mismatch defeats both formal confidence and measured accuracy.

**Known failures and misuses.** Constructed: independent x,y intervals lose the invariant x=y and cannot prove x−y=0. A soundiness tool ignoring eval can report no issues while eval executes a bad action. SAIL’s sampled loss alone is not its acceptance proof. Researcher checked the printed Fig.12 endpoint-only HardSwish fallback: for input[-3,0] it returns[0,0], but x=-3/2 maps exactly to -3/8. The formula is unsound on this domain. This does not reproduce a SAIL implementation failure or refute every generated transformer. Fig.8 also calls exact GeLU monotonic; endpoint bounds fail on[-2,0] at x=-1. No correction/author response was located in a targeted current search.

**Response or descendant form.** Reduced products, relational/context/path-sensitive domains and checked transfer-function generation improve precision selectively; underapproximating bug finders remain a different service.

**What changed and what did not.** Domain specialization and proof/checker-supported generation reduce some burdens; they do not remove precision tradeoffs or semantic-model responsibility.

**Residual limits.** No general effective complete analyzer; no broad independent evaluation of current LLM-generated transformer reliability or maintenance effort. The printed SAIL fallback is specifically counterexampled; current artifact behavior and author response remain unverified.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** A “sound analyzer” label or alarm count without coverage, assumptions and outcome taxonomy hides the mechanism.

**Internal tension ids.** EPLT-TB04

**Retention status.** ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVE

**Retention rationale.** Retain semantic soundness for proof-producing uses and explicitly separate pragmatic underapproximation; do not mandate maximal precision.

**Finding.** The normalized access-level enum contradicts the actual inspected portions in several records. SB034, SB039 and SB064 are labeled RELEVANT_SECTIONS_INSPECTED although each explicitly records only abstract/metadata access and failed body retrieval. Conversely SA030 is METADATA_ONLY even though its cited 1994 source theorem/definition sections were inspected; only the separately mentioned 1999 version was metadata-only. The aggregate access counts therefore are not counts of the stated source access. The explanatory normalization note does not repair an inaccurate machine value.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

**Finding id.** EPLT-AD006

**Finding.** Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** A rewrite is justified only for contexts satisfying its semantic premises and for the specific relation it promises to preserve; termination, confluence and profitability are additional obligations.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A program/IR transformation is claimed to preserve a semantic relation while replacing expressions or control flow.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Known non-trigger: No replacement of expressions/control is claimed to preserve a semantic relation; for example, text presentation changes are assessed only for a textual contract without behavioral preservation being asserted. Lower-cost option already recorded: For an infrequently executed pure expression, leave it unchanged; for formatting-only refactoring, a syntax-preservation check may suffice. **Environment and boundary.** One rewrite or pass within a named language; source-level arithmetic identities are not automatically target-level identities.

**What changed and what did not.** Semantic rule validation and richer effects/definedness models expose these cases; cost models and context coverage still require independent justification.

**Residual limits.** A correct local rule need not be profitable, and a valid rule set may have unbounded search or unsound composition through premises.

**Retention status.** STRONGLY_RETAINED

## EPLT-C0105 — Separate sound equality exploration from bounded extraction and optimization benefit

### Identity

**Property id.** EPLT-C0105

**Property name.** Separate sound equality exploration from bounded extraction and optimization benefit

**Lineage id.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY

**Property families.** B11 Equality saturation
