**Parent ids.** None recorded.

**Alias or supersession ids.** None recorded.

**Discovery source ids.** EPLT-SB021; EPLT-SB022; EPLT-SB023; EPLT-SB024; EPLT-SB019

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Tate et al.2009 formulated equality saturation to retain alternatives across transformations; egg2021 makes rebuilding/e-class analyses practical; egglog2023 integrates Datalog; Optimism2026 repairs a cyclic-analysis interaction.

**Original terminology.** E-graph; congruence closure; equality saturation; e-class analysis; extraction

**Original form.** Accumulate equivalences without destructively choosing a rewrite path, then extract a term according to a specified cost.

**Original problem.** Greedy pass ordering discards useful alternatives; uncontrolled saturation, unsound rules or a poor cost proxy can still defeat the desired optimization.

**Branch ids.** EPLT-BB03

**Influence or relation class.** REFINEMENT_OR_RESTRICTION

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** EPLT-SB019

**Locator.** Reduction order; overlap/critical pairs; completion limitations

**Source id.** EPLT-SB021

**Locator.** Equality-saturation representation and phase-ordering rationale

**Source id.** EPLT-SB022

**Locator.** Theorem 3.1 rebuilding; §4.3 extraction; §5 resource limits and bindings

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Do not project current features, proof coverage or terminology backwards onto earlier versions.

**Relation class explanation.** Detailed dated historical/analytical edges are in genealogy_edges; this record summarizes qualified present evolution and does not claim every cited source influenced every other source.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Equality saturation can explore many equivalent alternatives, but soundness requires valid equalities and analyses, and extraction quality is relative to represented candidates, cost model and resource limits.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_DESCRIPTIVE_AND_ENGINEERING

**Bearer or subject.** e-graph, rewrite/analysis system and extracted program

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Greedy pass ordering discards useful alternatives; uncontrolled saturation, unsound rules or a poor cost proxy can still defeat the desired optimization.

**Mechanism.** Maintain congruence classes, apply guarded equations, rebuild invariants, compute analyses and extract a low-cost representative under explicit limits.

**Mature or evolved form.** egglog supports interacting relational analyses; optimistic cyclic analyses require sound handling of well-formed represented graphs and cannot naively interleave tentative facts with irreversible equality merges.

**Expected payoff.** Reduce destructive phase-ordering losses and reuse equivalence information across optimization choices.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Published egg/egglog applications show performance/expressiveness benefits in their cases. Optimism2026 proves a specialized analysis result and evaluates generated programs; none establishes globally fastest code.

**Decision or consumer.** Optimizer designer balancing compile time, semantic validity and target-workload cost.

**Alternative mechanisms.** A short pass pipeline, bounded greedy rewriting, direct superoptimization in a finite space, or no optimization.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** Several interacting rewrites create a meaningful alternative space and the optimization objective justifies exploration.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Known non-trigger: The assessed task does not involve several interacting rewrites with meaningful alternatives and an optimization objective that calls for their exploration; for example, only one declared local rewrite is considered and no equality-saturation/global-search claim is made. Lower-cost option already recorded: For a tiny straight-line expression with one obviously safe local simplification, a terminating greedy rule or unchanged code is adequate. Applicability and evidence limit: One local rule may be adequate for its own transformation objective. If multi-rewrite exploration is actually claimed or performed, a small search space or unchanged extracted result leaves A true. A greedy rule does not establish a broader optimality claim without the corresponding evidence.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Every inserted equality is valid under the same semantics; analyses used in guards are sound; extraction handles cycles/binding correctly; cost domain and limits are specified.

**Environment and boundary.** E-graph representation and extracted term; target machine performance is a further empirical relation.

**Scope and exclusions.** Represented-equivalence validity and extraction under the chosen cost/search model. Excludes: Universal saturation termination, exhaustive semantic equivalence, global optimum over all programs, or runtime superiority from AST size.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Conditional semantic/mechanistic result. No universal mandate or legal authority is inferred.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Initial graph, rule premises, analysis version/convergence, rebuilding state, extraction proof/algorithm assumptions, budget and measured deployment cost if claimed.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** EPLT-C0104 validates rules; EPLT-C0103 validates analysis premises; EPLT-C0101 handles SSA/binding; EPLT-C0115 invalidates cached analysis after merges or semantic changes.

**Failure of assumptions.** One invalid equality poisons a class. Tentative optimistic facts used before convergence can justify irrevocable invalid merges; ill-formed cyclic represented graphs need special treatment.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Memory/time growth, scheduling, extraction complexity and representation of bindings/cycles can exceed the value of optimized execution.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Re-enter on rewrite set, analysis, cost function, binding representation, extraction strategy or budget change; retain old results only for their exact configuration.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** EPLT-KB05

**Strongest objection.** Avoiding destructive phase ordering does not abolish exploration-order, budget, representation or cost-model effects; e-class equality is only as sound as its derivation.

**Known failures and misuses.** Published Optimism2026 shows naive cyclic optimistic analysis can be unsound. Constructed: add x/x=1 without x≠0, then extract 1 at x=0; or choose fewer AST nodes that execute more slowly on the target.

**Response or descendant form.** egglog supports interacting relational analyses; optimistic cyclic analyses require sound handling of well-formed represented graphs and cannot naively interleave tentative facts with irreversible equality merges.

**What changed and what did not.** Rebuilding/relational analyses/optimistic repairs expand capability, while semantic premises and finite resource constraints remain.

**Residual limits.** No universal cost model or saturation bound; binding/effects/cycles remain representation-specific; current synthetic evaluation is not broad industrial replication.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** Counting rewrites, e-nodes or saturation iterations can reward search growth without valid or useful output.

**Internal tension ids.** EPLT-TB03

**Retention status.** CONTEXT_DEPENDENT

**Retention rationale.** Retain non-destructive exploration as a guarded mechanism; reject unconditional optimality and “rebuilding terminates therefore saturation terminates.”

## EPLT-C0106 — Instantiate compiler preservation at the exact semantic endpoints and premises

### Identity

**Property id.** EPLT-C0106

**Lineage id.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY

**Parent ids.** None recorded.

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** CompCert’s 2009 verified Cminor back end developed simulation proofs for a restricted pipeline. Current 3.18 composes a larger C-AST pipeline and includes a modeled separate-compilation theorem; trusted-boundary scrutiny evolves alongside it.

**Original terminology.** Backward simulation; behavior improvement; refinement; semantic preservation; successful compilation

**Original form.** Prove once that every successful application of a compiler function preserves an explicitly modeled relation.

**Original problem.** Compiler bugs introduce behaviors absent from a safe source; a true AST-level theorem is advertised as source-text-to-deployed-system correctness.

**Branch ids.** EPLT-BB04

**Influence or relation class.** REFINEMENT_OR_RESTRICTION

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** EPLT-SB013

**Locator.** §2.1 semantic preservation; §2.2 verified validators and certifying compilation

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Do not project current features, proof coverage or terminology backwards onto earlier versions.

**Relation class explanation.** Detailed dated historical/analytical edges are in genealogy_edges; this record summarizes qualified present evolution and does not claim every cited source influenced every other source.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** A compiler preservation theorem justifies only its stated source/target semantic relation for matching versions/configurations and satisfied premises; successful compilation and external intent are separate questions.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_DESCRIPTIVE_AND_ENGINEERING

**Bearer or subject.** CompCert source AST, generated assembly AST and preservation theorem

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Compiler bugs introduce behaviors absent from a safe source; a true AST-level theorem is advertised as source-text-to-deployed-system correctness.

**Mechanism.** Prove simulation for passes, compose them, derive behavior refinement under safety assumptions, and inventory every conversion between the theorem’s formal endpoints and the actual build/run.

**Mature or evolved form.** Current CompCert adds source passes and formal separate linking; verified validation can be embedded in the pipeline; TCB studies identify semantic/output obligations beyond internal pass proofs.

**Expected payoff.** Exclude modeled miscompilations across all successful inputs rather than only sampled tests.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Current formal theorem statements support the modeled guarantee. TCB case analysis and root Csmith EPLT-SR002 provide boundary/failure evidence; no lane-wide quantitative defect-rate comparison is claimed.

**Decision or consumer.** A user transferring a proved source property through a specific compiler invocation.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Per-run translation validation; restricted interpreter; differential testing where universal proof is unnecessary.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A source-level claim is being transferred to an artifact produced by a compiler whose preservation theorem is invoked.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Known non-trigger: No source claim is transferred to an artifact by invoking a compiler-preservation theorem; for example, the question concerns parsing only and makes no execution-correspondence claim. Lower-cost option already recorded: If the question only asks whether a file parses, a parser result is sufficient; importing a compiler-preservation theorem answers a different question. Applicability and evidence limit: An existing matching theorem can cheaply establish the applicable transfer once its fragment, configuration and environment premises are discharged. Not having inspected such a theorem while claiming that transfer yields UNKNOWN, not a false guard.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Compiler function returns OK; source and target ASTs/configurations match the theorem; source safety needed for plain refinement; external calls and machine model follow the specified environment.

**Environment and boundary.** CompCert 3.18 Csyntax AST to Asm AST. Modeled link_list theorem covers matching compiled unit lists; preprocessing/elaboration, assembly output and external tool/runtime realization require separate correspondence.

**Scope and exclusions.** Specified observable behavior and successful supported compilation. Excludes: Source requirement correctness, all C extensions/concurrency, timing/memory bounds, arbitrary hostile contexts, and universal source-text-to-physical-system proof.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Conditional semantic/mechanistic result. No universal mandate or legal authority is inferred.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Theorem/version identity, exact input/output/configuration, proof dependencies, successful result and evidence for source safety/FFI/model assumptions.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** EPLT-C0102 addresses source elaboration; EPLT-C0104 pass semantics; EPLT-C0108 validated passes; EPLT-C0110 linking/foreign assumptions; EPLT-C0116 runtime realization; EPLT-C0114 and EPLT-C0115 version currency.

**Failure of assumptions.** Model or output-printer discrepancy can invalidate a deployment claim while the pass theorem remains true. Source UB weakens the conclusion; an always-reject compiler is vacuously safe but unusable.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Formal semantics and per-pass proofs impose maintenance; supported features/configurations and compilation failures constrain use.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Recheck exact compiler release, proof artifact, flags, front end, assembler/linker, source features and external specification after change; do not transfer a theorem solely by product name.

**Response or descendant form.** Current CompCert adds source passes and formal separate linking; verified validation can be embedded in the pipeline; TCB studies identify semantic/output obligations beyond internal pass proofs.

**What changed and what did not.** Current theorem coverage includes modeled linking and expanded front-end passes; output/environment identity and intended requirements remain separate.

**Residual limits.** Model adequacy, extraction and real toolchain trust remain; no proof replay or binary correspondence certification in this research.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** A theorem badge without endpoint/premise matching may provide no applicable guarantee to the actual binary.

**Internal tension ids.** EPLT-TB01; EPLT-TB02

**Retention status.** STRONGLY_RETAINED

**Retention rationale.** The exact theorem is powerful and nontrivial; endpoint discipline prevents both dismissal of real coverage and inflation beyond it.

**Mechanism.** Prove per-IR passes and binary encoding, integrate GC/bignum relations, instantiate a machine configuration and evaluate the compiler within the logic for a certified bootstrap artifact.

**Mature or evolved form.** Composition with a verified processor model extends another boundary; current CakeML supports more targets than historical papers, each requiring the relevant theorem/configuration.

**Expected payoff.** Reduce unverified code-generation/runtime boundaries and attach a theorem to concrete generated bytes.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** CakeML backend theorem and bootstrap construction establish specific formal artifacts. GC proof and processor composition cover distinct layers; their combination does not prove vendor synthesis or physical hardware.

**Decision or consumer.** A consumer needing source-to-machine-code correspondence with the modeled runtime.

**Alternative mechanisms.** AST theorem plus trusted assembler; a small proved interpreter; validating final binaries; ordinary compiler/testing when sufficient.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** The assurance claim crosses from language source into encoded machine code and runtime behavior.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Known non-trigger: The assurance claim is confined to an abstract source/model result and does not cross into encoded machine code and runtime behavior; for example, only a mathematical evaluator is discussed with no concrete-execution assurance. Lower-cost option already recorded: For a tiny bounded expression language, a small interpreter with explicit integer/environment semantics can be sufficient without self-hosting or multiple verified backends. Applicability and evidence limit: A small interpreter reduces the implementation boundary but does not remove it when actual execution is claimed. Adequate evidence must establish the exact declared source-to-execution relation, including its applicable configuration/installation/external-call/resource premises. A different interpreter theorem is a separately identified relation, not automatic PASS for the specific CakeML compilation formula.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Compilation succeeds; source does not Fail (discharged by front-end theorem when applicable); backend/machine configs agree; generated bytes/data are installed correctly; FFI follows its abstract oracle; allowed resource failure is understood.

**Environment and boundary.** CakeML source/text frontend to machine bytes interpreted in a machine model, including verified GC/bignums; wrapper, installation, FFI, OS and physical hardware need their stated correspondence.

**Scope and exclusions.** Compiled behavior included in resource-extended source behaviors for the named architecture/configuration. Excludes: Guaranteed no OOM/stack failure, arbitrary external mutation, all hardware/toolchains, or intent correctness.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Conditional semantic/mechanistic result. No universal mandate or legal authority is inferred.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Concrete code/data, compilation theorem/bootstrapping proof, machine configuration, installation/FFI evidence and resource policy.

**Residual limits.** No automatic availability/timing guarantee; no validation here of a real installed executable/FPGA synthesis chain.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** Bootstrapping or target-count claims matter only when the actual artifact and theorem premises match the deployment claim.

**Internal tension ids.** EPLT-TB02

## EPLT-C0108 — Validate each translation under a sound checker and preserve inconclusive outcomes

### Identity

**Property id.** EPLT-C0108

**Property name.** Validate each translation under a sound checker and preserve inconclusive outcomes

**Lineage id.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY

**Property families.** B12 Translation validation

**Record kind.** GUARDED_ENGINEERING_PROPERTY

**Parent ids.** None recorded.

**Alias or supersession ids.** None recorded.

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Pnueli/Siegel/Singerman1998 introduced translation validation; Necula2000 implemented per-pass checks for GCC. Leroy formalized verified-validator architecture; Alive2 and MLIR tools instantiate richer IR semantics with bounded practical checking.

**Original terminology.** Translation validation; validator soundness; simulation invariant; bounded refinement

**Original form.** Check source/target correspondence for each compiler result instead of trusting or proving the optimizer that produced it.

**Original problem.** A changing or heuristic optimizer is difficult to verify wholesale; a validator’s timeout, incomplete inference or bounded search is mistaken for a universal pass.

**Branch ids.** EPLT-BB04

**Influence or relation class.** REFINEMENT_OR_RESTRICTION

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** EPLT-SB064

**Locator.** Founding translation-validation formulation

**Source id.** EPLT-SB026

**Locator.** Simulation relation; invariant inference; §5 results/limitations

**Source id.** EPLT-SB013

**Locator.** §2.1 semantic preservation; §2.2 verified validators and certifying compilation

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Do not project current features, proof coverage or terminology backwards onto earlier versions.

**Relation class explanation.** Detailed dated historical/analytical edges are in genealogy_edges; this record summarizes qualified present evolution and does not claim every cited source influenced every other source.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** A sound validator can justify the particular accepted source/target pair independently of translator correctness, but only for its modeled fragment and bounds; nonacceptance need not be a bug witness.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_DESCRIPTIVE_AND_ENGINEERING

**Bearer or subject.** source/target translation pair, validator and modeled execution scope

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** A changing or heuristic optimizer is difficult to verify wholesale; a validator’s timeout, incomplete inference or bounded search is mistaken for a universal pass.

**Mechanism.** Construct a relational verification condition or simulation invariant for the pair and check it using trusted/proved validation logic; separate SAT counterexample, UNSAT result, timeout and unsupported input.

**Mature or evolved form.** SMT-based definedness/memory-aware validators and semantic dialect tooling extend applicability; verified validators can be embedded within verified compilers.

**Expected payoff.** Permit aggressive/untrusted search while localizing semantic assurance in a checker.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Necula’s prototype and Alive2/MLIR campaigns report discovered transformation bugs. A checker-soundness theorem gives conditional pairwise assurance; campaign results do not prove the entire translator.

**Decision or consumer.** A build/optimizer pipeline deciding whether to accept one transformed artifact.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Once-proved translator; proof-carrying result; restricted identity/pass; finite testing with narrower confidence.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A concrete source/target pair is available and its preservation claim must be checked under a specified model.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Known non-trigger: No concrete source/target pair is the subject of a preservation check under a specified model; for example, the task records one artifact’s identity without a source-to-target preservation claim. Lower-cost option already recorded: If a transformation is identity and byte/AST identity is the entire required relation, direct equality may suffice; general relational solving is unnecessary. Applicability and evidence limit: For an identity translation, direct byte/AST equality can establish P cheaply if equality is the entire required relation under the same interpretation and configuration. A remains true for that preservation check. Equal syntax under differing semantics, incomplete feature coverage or missing interpretation is insufficient; use UNKNOWN when the required premises are unavailable.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Validator encoding and solver/checker are sound; all relevant semantics/features supported; bounds cover the quantified executions or conclusion explicitly remains bounded.

**Environment and boundary.** One validated pair/pass and its semantics; parser, downstream code generation and runtime may lie outside it.

**Scope and exclusions.** Accepted pair’s declared relation, with loop/resource bounds explicit. Excludes: Validator completeness, all-pass/all-program compiler correctness from sampled accepted pairs, or source requirement correctness.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Conditional semantic/mechanistic result. No universal mandate or legal authority is inferred.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Both artifacts, versioned semantics, validator soundness basis, solver outcome and bounds/unsupported-feature checks.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** EPLT-C0104 supplies relation/premises; EPLT-C0106 may trust a verified validator; EPLT-C0115 includes validator/model versions; EPLT-C0117 prevents finite-validation corpus inflation.

**Failure of assumptions.** Missing LLVM features or unrolling bounds can hide a counterexample; faulty memory/poison encoding can accept a bad pair; inference failure can reject a correct pair.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Per-translation solver cost and timeouts; model updates track IR evolution; failing closed can block compilation.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Revalidate when either artifact, IR semantics, validator, solver assumptions, flags or bounds change; do not reuse acceptance keyed only to source text.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** EPLT-KB08

**Strongest objection.** The checker may be the hard semantic component, and incomplete inference or bounded checking cannot be advertised as general proof merely because the translator was treated as untrusted.

**Known failures and misuses.** Constructed: two loops agree for the unroll bound but differ one iteration later. Published Alive2 explicitly bounds loops, so success cannot certify unbounded behavior without further reasoning.

**Response or descendant form.** SMT-based definedness/memory-aware validators and semantic dialect tooling extend applicability; verified validators can be embedded within verified compilers.

**What changed and what did not.** Detailed semantic models and verified validator components strengthen accepted-pair evidence; coverage and trust remain separate from solver success.

**Residual limits.** Solver/encoding/model trust and scalability; not every transformation admits efficient validation.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** A green validation dashboard loses meaning if UNSUPPORTED/TIMEOUT are collapsed into success or the checked pair is not the shipped pair.

**Internal tension ids.** EPLT-TB01

**Retention status.** STRONGLY_RETAINED

**Retention rationale.** Retain conditional checker-based assurance as an alternative to translator verification; preserve bounded and inconclusive outcomes.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** A proof-carrying artifact establishes only the checked proposition/policy for the exact code and initial/environment assumptions; safety certificates do not automatically establish source-target equivalence.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_DESCRIPTIVE_AND_ENGINEERING

**Bearer or subject.** target code, consumer policy, proof certificate and checker

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** A consumer must accept foreign code without trusting its producer; a valid proof for a weak policy can be mistaken for every desired property.

**Mechanism.** Generate a VC from code and policy, check a proof with explicit axioms and bind it to the code; the producer’s search/certifier can be untrusted if acceptance checking is sound.

**Mature or evolved form.** Typed low-level evidence and verified validators are alternative certificate forms; richer policies widen assurance only when their semantics and checker obligations are supplied.

**Expected payoff.** Move trust from a complex producer toward a smaller checkable interface and enable safe acceptance of untrusted code.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** PCC Theorem3.1 gives modeled memory-read safety and a conditional postcondition; TAL safety and compiler-architecture analysis establish related but different guarantees.

**Decision or consumer.** The code consumer defining an admissible safety policy.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Sandbox/runtime checking; typed bytecode verifier; translation validation; direct review for a small trusted routine.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** Code from an untrusted/complex producer is accepted on the basis of a proof or typed certificate.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Known non-trigger: Code from an untrusted or complex producer is not accepted on the basis of a proof or typed certificate; for example, a local constant is evaluated directly with no certificate-based acceptance claim. Lower-cost option already recorded: A fixed local constant expression with no foreign access needs no portable safety certificate; direct evaluation/review can suffice. Applicability and evidence limit: A small proof or direct certificate checker can cheaply establish the applicable policy claim. Direct evaluation without certificate-based acceptance is a different assurance target. The code being a constant or having no foreign access does not negate A if its acceptance still relies on a certificate.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Policy captures desired forbidden actions; VC generator and checker are sound; proof/axioms match exact code; execution satisfies initial and machine/environment premises.

**Environment and boundary.** Target-code policy theorem. Source meaning enters only if the certificate explicitly proves a correspondence relation.

**Scope and exclusions.** Encoded safety/postcondition under stated machine model. Excludes: Automatic confidentiality, termination, source fidelity, useful behavior or trusted distribution from a generic proof badge.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Conditional semantic/mechanistic result. No universal mandate or legal authority is inferred.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Exact code/VC/proof identities, checked theorem, policy semantics, checker/axioms and initial-state evidence.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** EPLT-C0106 and EPLT-C0108 distinguish compiler/pairwise claims; EPLT-C0111 adds adversarial context/security policies; EPLT-C0116 realizes machine model; EPLT-C0115 binds certificate to current code.

**Failure of assumptions.** A memory-safe program may intentionally disclose a secret through allowed I/O; a proof attached to altered bytes proves the wrong object.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Proof generation/size, policy specification, VC/checker trust and certificate/code binding maintenance.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Recheck on code, policy, checker, axioms, initial state or machine/environment change; retire certificates for unsupported policy versions.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** EPLT-KB09

**Strongest objection.** A small trusted checker does not rescue an inadequate policy or wrong code binding; proof possession alone is not source fidelity or useful behavior.

**Known failures and misuses.** Constructed: a certificate proving memory safety is accepted for code that prints a private value through authorized output; memory safety holds while confidentiality fails.

**Response or descendant form.** Typed low-level evidence and verified validators are alternative certificate forms; richer policies widen assurance only when their semantics and checker obligations are supplied.

**What changed and what did not.** Result-side evidence reduces producer trust; requirements/policy adequacy and executable correspondence remain.

**Residual limits.** Certificate generation/usability and policy completeness; no general minimal trusted-base claim for all implementations.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** A proof-object count or signed certificate without policy/code identity can be ceremonial.

**Internal tension ids.** None recorded.

**Retention status.** CONTEXT_DEPENDENT

**Retention rationale.** Retain consumer-defined checkable evidence, with explicit policy scope; choose cheaper containment or typing when adequate.

### Evidence limits and open questions

**Evidence ceiling.** The encoded target policy under checker/model/initial assumptions.

**Transferability limits.** Applicable to another language/tool only after re-establishing its semantics, relation, assumptions and implementation correspondence.

**Review findings and disposition.** **Review passes.** EPLT-RV01; EPLT-RV02

**Relevant findings.** **Finding id.** EPLT-AD006

**Finding.** Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

**Disposition.** CORRECTED_AND_RECHECKED

## EPLT-C0110 — Compose component claims only within the proved context and linking relation

### Identity

**Property id.** EPLT-C0110

**Property name.** Compose component claims only within the proved context and linking relation

**Lineage id.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY

**Property families.** B13 Modularity, linking and foreign interfaces

**Record kind.** GUARDED_ENGINEERING_PROPERTY

**Parent ids.** None recorded.

**Alias or supersession ids.** None recorded.

**Discovery source ids.** EPLT-SB033; EPLT-SB036; EPLT-SB034; EPLT-SB010; EPLT-SB058; EPLT-SB053

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Existential abstraction explains representation hiding; ML modules distinguish abstract and manifest types needed for separate checking. Multi-language semantics and Melocoton make language-boundary obligations explicit. CompCert supplies a separate-compilation theorem for its modeled unit/link relation.

**Original terminology.** Existential package; abstract/manifest type; signature; functor; contextual equivalence; linking; FFI wrapper

**Original form.** Hide representation behind an interface and allow clients to depend only on the interface’s justified operations and laws.

**Original problem.** Local type correctness and an unchanged exported signature do not ensure compatible ownership, layout, calling convention, exceptions, atomic mappings or behavior after linking.

**Branch ids.** EPLT-BB05

**Influence or relation class.** REFINEMENT_OR_RESTRICTION

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** EPLT-SB033

**Locator.** Introduction: information hiding versus behavioral specification

**Source id.** EPLT-SB036

**Locator.** Abstract versus manifest type equations; compilation-unit/module distinction

**Source id.** EPLT-SB034

**Locator.** Institutional abstract: boundary composition and abstraction of low-level details

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Do not project current features, proof coverage or terminology backwards onto earlier versions.

**Relation class explanation.** Detailed dated historical/analytical edges are in genealogy_edges; this record summarizes qualified present evolution and does not claim every cited source influenced every other source.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Substitution and separate compilation preserve a component claim only for the stated class of contexts, interface laws, linking semantics and foreign-runtime assumptions; textual interface identity alone is insufficient.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_DESCRIPTIVE_AND_ENGINEERING

**Bearer or subject.** component pair, its interface and the set of linkable source/target contexts

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Local type correctness and an unchanged exported signature do not ensure compatible ownership, layout, calling convention, exceptions, atomic mappings or behavior after linking.

**Mechanism.** Relate implementations at an abstract interface, quantify over permitted contexts, and discharge link/FFI invariants. Type equalities, rooting, ownership and memory/exception conventions are explicit premises, not implied by a file/module name.

**Mature or evolved form.** Manifest-type modules support separate checking; contextual/logical relations and mixed-language separation logic express behavioral obligations. CompCert modeled linking and Melocoton wrapper adequacy give different, precise composition results.

**Expected payoff.** Local reasoning can survive replacement and mixed-language assembly without re-proving every client, when the contract covers the boundary behavior.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** CompCert’s separate_transf_c_program_correct quantifies over pairwise-compiled units and a successful source link. Melocoton Theorems4.1/4.2 compose language-local reasoning and give mixed-program safety/conditional postconditions. MixTesting provides a concrete failure of an omitted atomic-ABI obligation.

**Decision or consumer.** A linker, component integrator or client relying on a replacement module/plugin/foreign library.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Whole-program verification; a single-language implementation; copying/serialization boundary; runtime wrapper checks; rebuilding all components under one compatible configuration.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A correctness claim crosses a component, version, language, dynamically loaded plugin or separately compiled unit boundary.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Known non-trigger: No correctness claim crosses any component, version, language, dynamically loaded plugin or separately compiled-unit boundary; for example, a closed whole-program claim has no such cross-boundary inference. Lower-cost option already recorded: A closed sequential program with no separately replaceable or foreign component needs no general hostile-context theorem; direct whole-program checking can be adequate. Applicability and evidence limit: A small interface, restricted context class or complete whole-program argument can cheaply discharge an applicable composition claim if it covers the exact declared relation. A closed sequential program can still contain component/version boundaries; lack of hostile contexts does not itself negate this guard.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Context obeys the declared interface laws and ownership; link succeeds under the modeled rules; ABI/layout/exception/rooting/atomic conventions agree; any foreign implementation realizes the wrapper semantics.

**Environment and boundary.** Source module/type abstraction, modeled source/assembly linking, and explicit mixed OCaml-like/C-like language wrappers. Dynamic loading is covered only by a model that includes its new contexts and lifetime changes.

**Scope and exclusions.** The proved context class and exact link/wrapper semantics, with resulting safety or observable equivalence stated separately. Excludes: Arbitrary native libraries, unmodeled loader/symbol interposition, actual OCaml-runtime conformance, exceptions and multithreading omitted by Melocoton, and all algebraic interface laws from types alone.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Conditional semantic/mechanistic result. No universal mandate or legal authority is inferred.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Exact interface and behavioral laws, context class, successful modeled link, representation/FFI proof, ABI/configuration identities and correspondence to the actual loader/runtime.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** EPLT-C0106 supplies modeled separate compilation; EPLT-C0111 enlarges the context class adversarially; EPLT-C0112 supplies memory/atomic compatibility; EPLT-C0114–EPLT-C0115 govern version/context change; EPLT-C0116 supplies runtime realization.

**Failure of assumptions.** An unchanged signature can conceal a changed representation/ownership contract. A C callback may keep an unregistered managed pointer across moving GC. Individually correct atomic compiler mappings may be incompatible when mixed.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Behavioral contract specification, relation proofs, ABI matrices and wrapper/root maintenance; whole-program restrictions can reduce this cost.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Recheck on interface laws, implementation representation, loader policy, ABI, GC/root API, memory model, exception semantics, compiler configuration or foreign dependency change.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** EPLT-KB10

**Strongest objection.** Representation hiding and local correctness do not automatically compose across richer contexts; the boundary obligations are often exactly where supposedly modular assurances stop.

**Known failures and misuses.** Published: MixTesting Example1.1 combines individually correct Armv7-style loads and Armv8-style stores, admitting the both-zero store-buffering result forbidden by the source SC atomics. Constructed FFI variant: an unregistered C pointer becomes stale after a moving collection.

**Response or descendant form.** Manifest-type modules support separate checking; contextual/logical relations and mixed-language separation logic express behavioral obligations. CompCert modeled linking and Melocoton wrapper adequacy give different, precise composition results.

**What changed and what did not.** Explicit contexts and wrapper logics make the missing obligations visible and provable. They do not automatically supply behavioral laws or implementation correspondence for every existing FFI.

**Residual limits.** Incomplete actual-ABI/runtime models, especially exceptions, direct runtime-block pointers, concurrency and dynamic loading; empirical integration-cost comparisons not found.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** A module count, matching header or exported symbol list is inadequate evidence of the behavioral relation used by the client.

**Internal tension ids.** EPLT-TB05

**Retention status.** RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM

**Retention rationale.** Retain contextual substitution and explicit composition obligations; reject the stronger signature-alone inference.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Secure compilation requires a property class, attacker contexts and observations matched to the intended threat. Trace preservation, full abstraction and hyperproperty preservation are distinct criteria with different quantifier strength.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_DESCRIPTIVE_AND_ENGINEERING

**Bearer or subject.** source component, compiled component, attacker context class and security observation model

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Ordinary functional correspondence can omit hostile contexts or attacker-visible timing/address traces; therefore it need not preserve confidentiality or component isolation.

**Mechanism.** Prove every relevant target attack/observation has a permitted source explanation (back-translation), or use suitable simulation/logical-relational arguments; enforce target protection and account for compromise/leakage explicitly.

**Mature or evolved form.** Robust property hierarchies distinguish trace-level and whole-behavior-set criteria. SECOMP adds compartment-aware traces and dynamic compromise; leakage-sensitive simulations preserve noninterference; RobustDimSum composes robust-safety results via semantic back-translation into a capability target.

**Expected payoff.** A verified source security invariant can survive linking with modeled untrusted target components.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Formal conditional criteria and model-specific proofs exist. SECOMP extended paper states Theorem8.1 for bounded prefixes and an axiomatized/tested backtranslation-success assumption; the current artifact remains unintegrated with noted admits. RobustDimSum’s 2026 model theorem does not certify a physical CHERI toolchain.

**Decision or consumer.** A component owner relying on isolation, noninterference or robust safety after compilation and linking with untrusted code.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Single-language trusted contexts; OS/process isolation; explicit sandbox/capability wrapper; a narrower safety property if it captures the actual risk.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A required property must hold after an adversarial or more expressive target context interacts with compiled components.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Known non-trigger: No required property is asserted against an adversarial or more expressive target context interacting with compiled components; for example, only closed ordinary functional behavior in the stated trusted context is claimed. Lower-cost option already recorded: If every linked component is trusted and the claim is ordinary functional behavior, ordinary contextual/whole-program correspondence can be adequate; a full hostile-context theorem adds no automatic value. Applicability and evidence limit: Restricting the actual context/threat model can reduce the needed proof. A trusted context can still be more expressive than the source; if either triggering context condition remains, A is true and the chosen robust property needs its exact evidence. Ordinary functional correspondence alone does not prove a surviving security claim.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Exact attacker authority, allowed interfaces, observation/leakage model, target protection mechanisms and source well-formedness; every proof axiom, trace bound and compromise rule is part of the claim.

**Environment and boundary.** SECOMP: compartment-aware Clight-to-extended-RISC-V block-memory security model, scalar cross-compartment values and bounded trace prefixes. Noninterference and RobustDimSum use their own modeled languages and leakage/capability assumptions.

**Scope and exclusions.** Chosen robust property class within admitted source/target contexts and observations. Excludes: All side channels, physical target enforcement, arbitrary shared pointers, universal confidentiality from robust trace safety, and a fully integrated current SECOMP proof without admits.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Conditional semantic/mechanistic result. No universal mandate or legal authority is inferred.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Chosen security criterion, explicit attacker/observation models, proved theorem with axioms and bounds, versioned artifact status, and actual target enforcement correspondence.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** EPLT-C0110 states contexts/linking; EPLT-C0106 functional preservation is a related but insufficient premise; EPLT-C0109 target safety certificates need a security policy; EPLT-C0116 realizes isolation; EPLT-C0114–EPLT-C0115 track artifact and model changes.

**Failure of assumptions.** A target can preserve functional return values while exposing a secret through modeled-as-invisible address/timing behavior. A nominal compartment can fail if target contexts can modify protected stack or authority state.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Backtranslation/simulation proof burden, security-aware ABIs and runtime mechanisms, restrictions on cross-boundary values, and performance/engineering tradeoffs dependent on target.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Reassess on attacker authority, leakage observations, interfaces, shared-memory rules, target enforcement, compiler passes, trace bounds, proof axioms or artifact version change.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** EPLT-KB11

**Strongest objection.** The security name can conceal a weak property class, absent side channels or unproved enforcement. Full abstraction and robust safety are not interchangeable certificates of every security property.

**Known failures and misuses.** Constructed: a compiler preserves return values but converts a constant-time access into secret-dependent indexing; functional outputs agree while the attacker’s address trace distinguishes secrets. Published artifact-status counterexample: citing SECOMP’s paper theorem as a current fully integrated proof ignores admitted gaps documented in its README.

**Response or descendant form.** Robust property hierarchies distinguish trace-level and whole-behavior-set criteria. SECOMP adds compartment-aware traces and dynamic compromise; leakage-sensitive simulations preserve noninterference; RobustDimSum composes robust-safety results via semantic back-translation into a capability target.

**What changed and what did not.** Explicit criteria and semantic back-translation clarify what can be composed; newer simulations address leakage that functional proofs omit. They retain model scope and do not erase current artifact gaps.

**Residual limits.** Unmodeled physical leakage, practical shared pointers/FFIs, completeness of current proof integration, and deployment-specific enforcement/cost.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** A secure/fully abstract compiler badge without context, leakage and proof-status fields does not identify the preserved guarantee.

**Internal tension ids.** EPLT-TB05

**Retention status.** ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVE

**Retention rationale.** Retain criterion-specific robust preservation; explicitly withhold broad all-security and fully integrated artifact claims.

A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

## EPLT-C0112 — Evaluate concurrent transformations in the stated event and memory model

### Identity

**Property id.** EPLT-C0112

**Property name.** Evaluate concurrent transformations in the stated event and memory model

**Lineage id.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY

**Property families.** B14 Concurrent execution and weak memory

**Record kind.** GUARDED_ENGINEERING_PROPERTY

**Parent ids.** None recorded.

**Alias or supersession ids.** None recorded.

**Discovery source ids.** EPLT-SB037; EPLT-SB038; EPLT-SB039; EPLT-SB040; EPLT-SB041; EPLT-SB042; EPLT-SB053; EPLT-SB062; EPLT-SB065; EPLT-SB066

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** CSP’s synchronous communicating processes, actor-style asynchronous messages and event structures retain different interaction information. Lamport specifies processor-memory SC; Herlihy/Wing define object-history linearizability. C/C++ weak-memory formalizations, Promising and IMM address compiler mapping legality; MixTesting exposes mixed-mapping composition.

**Original terminology.** Trace; interleaving; partial order; causality; happens-before; reads-from; coherence; linearization; promise certification

**Original form.** Give concurrent executions a precise admissibility relation rather than infer outcomes from source textual order.

**Original problem.** A sequentially valid reorder or independently correct mapping can admit forbidden concurrent observations under interference, weak memory or incompatible separately compiled units.

**Branch ids.** EPLT-BB06

**Influence or relation class.** REFINEMENT_OR_RESTRICTION

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** EPLT-SB038

**Locator.** Guarded commands; synchronous I/O; §7.2 libraries; §7.4 buffering

**Source id.** EPLT-SB037

**Locator.** Sequential consistency definition; counterexample and requirements R1/R2

**Source id.** EPLT-SB039

**Locator.** Act3; asynchronous messages; dynamic state and reconfiguration

**Source id.** EPLT-SB065

**Locator.** §2 history semantics; legal sequential history; real-time order and locality

**Source id.** EPLT-SB062

**Locator.** Interleavings; causal independence; event structure configurations; relation to domains

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Do not project current features, proof coverage or terminology backwards onto earlier versions.

**Relation class explanation.** Detailed dated historical/analytical edges are in genealogy_edges; this record summarizes qualified present evolution and does not claim every cited source influenced every other source.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Transformation correctness is relative to specified memory/event semantics and observables. SC, linearizability, causal partial orders and message-passing traces are different relations; their guarantees cannot be exchanged by name.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_DESCRIPTIVE_AND_ENGINEERING

**Bearer or subject.** concurrent program or object history and its source/target event models

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** A sequentially valid reorder or independently correct mapping can admit forbidden concurrent observations under interference, weak memory or incompatible separately compiled units.

**Mechanism.** Define valid execution graphs/histories, preserve the required source-to-target outcome relation and prove mapping compatibility. Distinguish operation invocation/response order from individual memory events and hidden propagation steps.

**Mature or evolved form.** Promising uses certifiable thread-local promises; IMM provides a mechanized intermediate weak-memory model and corrected mapping results. Atomic-ABI analysis addresses mixing. A 2021 correction repairs the pending-invocation condition in the original linearizability definition.

**Expected payoff.** Expose source-forbidden outcomes and justify optimizations/mappings without assuming all concurrent executions are simple source-order interleavings.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Model-specific mapping/simulation theorems and mechanized IMM results; published litmus counterexamples for mixing; corrected linearizability locality proof. These are stronger than a finite litmus pass but do not cover unmodeled optimizations or hardware behavior.

**Decision or consumer.** Compiler optimizer/backend author, atomic-library integrator or concurrent-object verifier.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Use a sequential protocol, stronger atomics/locks with an adequate proof, or a single consistent atomic mapping; choose a simpler model when it satisfies the required observations.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** Concurrent interference or asynchronous interaction can affect externally visible results, or a translation changes atomic/event ordering.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Known non-trigger: Neither concurrent/asynchronous interference affecting visible results nor a translation change to atomic/event ordering is present; for example, the assessed computation is genuinely isolated and sequential with no such ordering change. Lower-cost option already recorded: A genuinely isolated sequential computation with no concurrent shared access can be checked in its sequential semantics; a weak-memory framework is unnecessary. Applicability and evidence limit: A small lock, direct interleaving argument or complete finite model check can cheaply establish the applicable declared concurrency relation. A simple program remains applicable if shared interference or changed atomic/event order affects the claim.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Named language/ISA memory models, atomic modes, race/undefined-behavior premises, graph consistency, compatible ABI mappings and explicit observation relation. Linearizability uses well-formed histories and a legal sequential object specification with corrected pending-operation handling.

**Environment and boundary.** Source concurrent semantics through modeled instruction mapping; actual hardware, arbitrary optimizations and mixed compiler/library versions need additional evidence.

**Scope and exclusions.** Outcome/history refinement for the declared language/model pair and transformation fragment. Excludes: All DRF code being SC despite relaxed atomics, global liveness from safety, arbitrary compiler optimizations from IMM instruction-mapping proofs, or all actor/session semantics from one model.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Conditional semantic/mechanistic result. No universal mandate or legal authority is inferred.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Versioned source/target models, complete operation mappings, definedness/race assumptions, simulation/mapping proof or scoped counterexample, and mixed-unit configuration.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** EPLT-C0104 rewrite side conditions become interference-sensitive; EPLT-C0110 requires atomic ABI compatibility; EPLT-C0113 adds fairness/liveness; EPLT-C0116 relates model to executed implementation.

**Failure of assumptions.** Plain data races may yield source UB rather than a well-defined litmus outcome. Mixing SC and weak accesses can invalidate a mapping argument. A history definition that ignores pending invocations can claim locality for the wrong relation.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** State/graph complexity, architecture/version-specific models and proofs, reduced optimization freedom or stronger synchronization overhead.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Recheck on memory model, atomic lowering, compiler options, architecture, synchronization library, race assumptions, observation granularity or history-definition revision.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** EPLT-KB12

**Strongest objection.** Elegant local or sequential reasoning is unreliable if the actual event/memory model, pending operations or composition ABI is omitted; model correctness is not hardware validation.

**Known failures and misuses.** Published: MixTesting’s Armv7-load/Armv8-store mixture permits both0 despite each uniform mapping’s correctness. Published correction: a read returning1 before a later pending write1 is admitted by the literal old linearizability formula but rejected by the amended one. These are distinct failures.

**Response or descendant form.** Promising uses certifiable thread-local promises; IMM provides a mechanized intermediate weak-memory model and corrected mapping results. Atomic-ABI analysis addresses mixing. A 2021 correction repairs the pending-invocation condition in the original linearizability definition.

**What changed and what did not.** Mechanized intermediate models and explicit atomic compatibility repair particular mapping arguments. They do not yield a universal strongest concurrency model or remove synchronization/proof costs.

**Residual limits.** Actual hardware/model conformance, optimized mixed-language code, full actor primary-text access and the rapidly changing range of language/ISA features.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** A data-race-free/linearizable/thread-safe label without the associated theorem, memory model and progress scope is under-specified.

**Internal tension ids.** EPLT-TB06

**Retention status.** STRONGLY_RETAINED

**Retention rationale.** Retain model-specific concurrent meaning and composition checks; reject substitution of source order or a safety label for the proved relation.

## EPLT-C0113 — State scheduling, memory and environment assumptions for each temporal guarantee

### Identity

**Property id.** EPLT-C0113

**Property name.** State scheduling, memory and environment assumptions for each temporal guarantee

**Lineage id.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY

**Property families.** B14 Temporal meaning, progress and fairness

**Record kind.** GUARDED_ENGINEERING_PROPERTY

**Parent ids.** None recorded.

**Alias or supersession ids.** None recorded.

**Discovery source ids.** EPLT-SB038; EPLT-SB043; EPLT-SB052; EPLT-SB062; EPLT-SB065; EPLT-SB066

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Process semantics distinguish available transitions from complete system behavior. Linearizability’s nonblocking property concerns existence of a valid response extension, not scheduler progress. Weak-memory fairness work exposes internal propagation obligations; 2026 liveness rules extend helpful-transition/ranking reasoning to RA and Strong Coherence.

**Original terminology.** Safety; local progress; deadlock freedom; termination; starvation freedom; fairness; response property; helpful transition

**Original form.** Reason about what eventually happens, not only whether an observed finite prefix avoids an error.

**Original problem.** A well-typed or non-stuck component can wait forever; a fair thread scheduler can still admit forever-stale reads if internal memory propagation is unfair.

**Branch ids.** EPLT-BB06

**Influence or relation class.** REFINEMENT_OR_RESTRICTION

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** EPLT-SB038

**Locator.** Guarded commands; synchronous I/O; §7.2 libraries; §7.4 buffering

**Source id.** EPLT-SB062

**Locator.** Interleavings; causal independence; event structure configurations; relation to domains

**Source id.** EPLT-SB065

**Locator.** §2 history semantics; legal sequential history; real-time order and locality

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Do not project current features, proof coverage or terminology backwards onto earlier versions.

**Relation class explanation.** Detailed dated historical/analytical edges are in genealogy_edges; this record summarizes qualified present evolution and does not claim every cited source influenced every other source.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Each liveness/progress statement needs its own trace quantifier and scheduling, memory and environment assumptions. Local progress, global deadlock freedom, starvation freedom and termination are distinct claims.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_DESCRIPTIVE_AND_ENGINEERING

**Bearer or subject.** possibly infinite execution trace under a scheduler, memory model and environment

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** A well-typed or non-stuck component can wait forever; a fair thread scheduler can still admit forever-stale reads if internal memory propagation is unfair.

**Mechanism.** Define fair executions, include internal memory actions where needed, and prove response/termination through invariants and well-founded progress measures. Separate a safety relation from a temporal completion guarantee.

**Mature or evolved form.** Declarative weak-memory fairness uses prefix-finiteness of appropriate coherence/from-read relations and corresponds to operational fairness in specified models. 2026 work adds helpful internal memory transitions and potential/ranking rules for RA/Strong Coherence examples.

**Expected payoff.** Identify the precise premise that turns an allowed infinite wait into a required response, avoiding false assurance from a local safety theorem.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Fairness2021 proves model-specific operational/declarative correspondences and studies lock termination. The 2026 paper proves rule soundness and ticket-lock starvation freedom under its hypotheses; it does not establish bounded response time for arbitrary runtimes.

**Decision or consumer.** A language/protocol verifier or optimizer whose claim includes completion, responsiveness or fair infinite behavior.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Finite sequential state machine, bounded timeout with explicitly weaker failure semantics, or safety-only claim when eventual service is not required.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** The desired result includes eventual response, global progress, termination or preservation of infinite-execution behavior.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Known non-trigger: The desired result includes none of eventual response, global progress, termination, or preservation of infinite-execution behavior; for example, only a finite-prefix safety property is claimed and no eventual-completion conclusion is drawn. Lower-cost option already recorded: For a terminating finite straight-line sequential computation, elementary bounded evaluation can establish completion without fairness machinery. Applicability and evidence limit: Completion of a deterministic finite straight-line computation can be established by adequate bounded execution or a direct finite argument, with coverage matching the claimed inputs and environment. This is PASS for an applicable termination claim. An unfinished finite prefix, sampled inputs or absent environment assumptions do not establish unbounded liveness and yield UNKNOWN for that wider claim.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Scheduler fairness notion, internal memory-propagation fairness, environment/peer responsiveness, enabledness rules and a valid well-founded ranking or response proof. Fairness does not impose a numeric latency bound.

**Environment and boundary.** The modeled transition system and its fair infinite executions. Operating-system scheduling, network delivery and physical timing are outside unless explicitly related.

**Scope and exclusions.** The named response/progress property for traces satisfying all fairness and environment assumptions. Excludes: Real-time deadlines, unconditional termination of all well-typed programs, and implementation lock freedom from linearizability alone.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Conditional semantic/mechanistic result. No universal mandate or legal authority is inferred.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Transition model, exact temporal formula, enabledness/fairness assumptions, environment contract and invariant/ranking/response proof. Finite traces alone cannot establish an unbounded eventuality.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** EPLT-C0112 supplies the execution model; EPLT-C0110 supplies peer/interface obligations; EPLT-C0116 supplies runtime scheduling/propagation correspondence; EPLT-C0114 changes can invalidate fairness assumptions.

**Failure of assumptions.** A writer runs once and a reader runs infinitely but repeatedly sees stale0 if memory fairness is absent; an environment never sends a required message; a scheduler never runs an enabled component.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Fairness-sensitive temporal proofs, infinite-state reasoning, ranking design and potential runtime synchronization/latency costs.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Revalidate when scheduling policy, memory model/fairness, environment obligations, synchronization, enabledness or progress measure changes.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** EPLT-KB13

**Strongest objection.** Fairness can hide precisely the executions that cause practical failures, and a safety/progress label can be inflated into an eventuality unsupported by the theorem.

**Known failures and misuses.** Source-grounded mechanism, small constructed trace: after x is written1, a scheduled reader repeatedly loads old0 forever; thread fairness holds, but omitted memory fairness allows nontermination. The 1990 linearizability paper explicitly permits implementations to block or deadlock despite its specification-level nonblocking property.

**Response or descendant form.** Declarative weak-memory fairness uses prefix-finiteness of appropriate coherence/from-read relations and corresponds to operational fairness in specified models. 2026 work adds helpful internal memory transitions and potential/ranking rules for RA/Strong Coherence examples.

**What changed and what did not.** Explicit memory fairness and helpful-transition rules close a genuine logical gap for specified models; they do not establish external scheduling promises or latency bounds.

**Residual limits.** Whether real environments satisfy assumptions, proof scalability and fair-transformation preservation beyond the studied models.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** A progress/deadlock-free label without the exact conclusion, fairness class and environment contract is not enough to justify responsiveness.

**Internal tension ids.** EPLT-TB06

**Retention status.** ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVE

**Retention rationale.** Retain temporal guarantees with explicit premises; prevent safety-to-liveness promotion and vacuous exclusion of relevant executions.

## EPLT-C0114 — Define compatibility as an explicit relation over versions, consumers and observations

### Identity

**Property id.** EPLT-C0114

**Property name.** Define compatibility as an explicit relation over versions, consumers and observations

**Lineage id.** EVOLVED_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_THEORY

**Property families.** B20 Language, schema and IR evolution

**Record kind.** GUARDED_ENGINEERING_PROPERTY

**Parent ids.** None recorded.

**Alias or supersession ids.** None recorded.

**Discovery source ids.** EPLT-SB044; EPLT-SB045; EPLT-SB046; EPLT-SB059; EPLT-SB060; EPLT-SB061; EPLT-SB055

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Language migrations such as Python’s division change exposed the gap between unchanged grammar and unchanged meaning. Semantic Versioning specifies a declared-API convention. Protobuf and LLVM articulate distinct wire/IR compatibility policies; evolving mechanized Wasm developments show proof/artifact currency is another dimension.

**Original terminology.** Backward/forward compatibility; migration; deprecation; version negotiation; wire safety; semantic versioning; replay

**Original form.** Signal and manage breaking changes so consumers can coordinate upgrades and preserve intended uses.

**Original problem.** A parsable old artifact, unchanged source string or compatible wire encoding can change behavior or invalidate proofs; version labels cannot themselves establish semantic compatibility.

**Branch ids.** EPLT-BB07

**Influence or relation class.** REFINEMENT_OR_RESTRICTION

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Source id.** EPLT-SB045

**Locator.** Classic/true/floor division; future directive and migration warnings

**Source id.** EPLT-SB044

**Locator.** Rules 1, 3, 6–8, 10; public API and immutable releases

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Do not project current features, proof coverage or terminology backwards onto earlier versions.

**Relation class explanation.** Detailed dated historical/analytical edges are in genealogy_edges; this record summarizes qualified present evolution and does not claim every cited source influenced every other source.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Compatibility must name the version pair, direction, consumer class and preserved observations/obligations. Migration or deliberate breakage requires revalidation of those claims, independently of syntax and version numbering.

**Claim class.** CONDITIONAL_DESCRIPTIVE_AND_ENGINEERING

**Bearer or subject.** old/new language or schema versions, migration and affected consumer/evidence obligations

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** A parsable old artifact, unchanged source string or compatible wire encoding can change behavior or invalidate proofs; version labels cannot themselves establish semantic compatibility.

**Mechanism.** Specify a migration/upgrade relation, preserve historical version identity, identify changed defaults and dependencies, and test/prove consumer-specific obligations across mixed-version states.

**Mature or evolved form.** Explicit feature/edition negotiation, staged rollout restrictions, reserved schema identifiers, IR-upgrade policies and proof-maintenance architectures distinguish several meanings of compatibility.

**Expected payoff.** Avoid silent reinterpretation and identify which consumers/evidence must change, without requiring all future semantics to preserve every old behavior.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** PEP238 gives a concrete same-syntax meaning change and migration mechanisms. Protobuf documents wire-compatible changes that still break generated code or truncate values. LLVM explicitly distinguishes textual IR and bitcode commitments. These normative cases establish mechanisms, not a universal quantified migration theorem.

**Decision or consumer.** Library/language/schema maintainers and downstream consumers deciding whether old artifacts and evidence remain valid.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Freeze the old interpreter/schema, reject unknown versions, use an explicit breaking-version boundary, or manually migrate a small finite artifact population.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A language, IR, schema, library, default, runtime or toolchain changes while old source/data/artifacts or evidence remain in use.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** Known non-trigger: No change is being judged while old source, data, artifacts or evidence remain in use, and no old-to-new compatibility obligation is claimed; for example, all old artifacts are actually retired and only a fresh single-version claim is assessed. Lower-cost option already recorded: For a small isolated disposable artifact set, regenerate and recheck everything under one version; sophisticated mixed-version compatibility machinery may cost more than full migration. Applicability and evidence limit: Full regeneration and rechecking can remove a reuse obligation once old artifacts and claims are actually retired. If old-to-new compatibility is still required, A remains true; checking the new version alone does not prove the required old-to-new observation relation.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Old/new version identities are stable; relevant consumers and observations are declared; the migration relation handles admitted artifacts; rollout restrictions and environment/library dependencies are followed.

**Environment and boundary.** Specified version pair and consumer class, including generated code, wire data, old readers/new writers and any proof/checker artifacts.

**Scope and exclusions.** Syntactic acceptance, wire decoding, semantic behavior and evidence validity are separately named relations; only the chosen ones are required. Excludes: Automatic compatibility from a major/minor label, universal old/new interoperability, or preservation of obsolete behavior when a deliberate documented breaking change is intended.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Conditional semantic/mechanistic result. No universal mandate or legal authority is inferred.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Exact semantic/schema/tool versions; changed-default inventory; consumers/rollout states; migration definition and property-specific tests/proofs; separately current evidence/checker versions.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** EPLT-C0110 interface/context changes; EPLT-C0115 evidence invalidation; EPLT-C0101 IR identity; EPLT-C0116 runtime semantics; EPLT-C0106/EPLT-C0111 theorem/artifact version matching.

**Failure of assumptions.** Same expression 3/2 returns integer1 under Python2 classic integer division and1.5 under Python3 true division. Adding an enum value can be wire-safe yet break exhaustive consumer source; widening protobuf int32 to int64 can truncate for old readers.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Consumer inventory, migration tools/tests, mixed-version rollout and retained historical artifacts; stronger compatibility can constrain language improvement.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Re-evaluate on any semantic dependency/default/feature-policy change; retire old evidence explicitly rather than rewriting its historical meaning. A syntactic edit need not invalidate a property if a relevant invariance proof exists.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** EPLT-KB14

**Strongest objection.** Semantic Versioning and grammar/schema compatibility can communicate useful constraints while leaving the actual consumer’s semantics unproved; preserving everything can also block legitimate evolution.

**Known failures and misuses.** Published normative examples: wire-safe enum addition can break exhaustive generated-client handling; old int32 readers can truncate newly permitted int64 values. Constructed stale proof: a proof using floor division is reused for identical text under true division.

**Response or descendant form.** Explicit feature/edition negotiation, staged rollout restrictions, reserved schema identifiers, IR-upgrade policies and proof-maintenance architectures distinguish several meanings of compatibility.

**What changed and what did not.** Explicit consumer/direction/rollout relations replace one compatibility label with testable obligations; intentional changes still require updated intent and evidence rather than forced old behavior.

**Residual limits.** Unknown consumers, unspecified intended meaning and cost of proof migration; full current Progressful Interpreters PDF was not recovered, so no detailed benchmark conclusion is used.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** A semantic-version label or unchanged interface signature is not proof that every behavior/evidence obligation survives.

**Internal tension ids.** EPLT-TB07

**Retention status.** STRONGLY_RETAINED

**Retention rationale.** Retain explicit semantic/consumer compatibility and historical identity; reject syntax/version-number proxies.

**P.** ∀p∈AdmittedOld ∀C∈Consumers. Defined(migrate(p),C) ∧ ObsNew(C,migrate(p)) R ObsOld(C,p). SyntaxAccepted or WireDecodable is a weaker separate predicate; a version label is evidence of a policy commitment, not a proof of this formula.

**Change invalidation rule.** Re-evaluate on any semantic dependency/default/feature-policy change; retire old evidence explicitly rather than rewriting its historical meaning. A syntactic edit need not invalidate a property if a relevant invariance proof exists.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Consumer inventory, migration tools/tests, mixed-version rollout and retained historical artifacts; stronger compatibility can constrain language improvement. Cheaper path: For a small isolated disposable artifact set, regenerate and recheck everything under one version; sophisticated mixed-version compatibility machinery may cost more than full migration. Applicability and evidence limit: Full regeneration and rechecking can remove a reuse obligation once old artifacts and claims are actually retired. If old-to-new compatibility is still required, A remains true; checking the new version alone does not prove the required old-to-new observation relation.

**Evidence ceiling.** Documented policy and consumer-specific checked/proved relation, not universal semantics preservation from release labels.

**Formalisation provenance.** Researcher operational compatibility obligation synthesized from official migration/version policies; not attributed as a proved universal theorem to those documents.

**Operational evaluation.** Compare meanings in old/new environments; exercise mixed-version consumers and boundary values; check whether existing theorem assumptions are still true. Unknown consumers mean unknown general compatibility. No target implementation was supplied or certified by this research. A/P/E are evaluation obligations, not computed owner-system scores.
